identification: Four miniature vaseline (uranium, yellow) pressed glass animal-on-nest covered salt dishes, about 6-8 cm long: a cat on nest, a hen on nest, a turkey on nest and a dog (Scottie/terrier type) on nest, each with a scalloped basketweave base. These are the 'hen on nest' style novelty salts made in the 1970s-2000s by US makers such as Boyd, Degenhart, Mosser, Summit and Westmoreland, not Victorian. Plus two vaseline glass eye baths (eye wash cups): one clear vaseline with banded rim on a short pedestal, and one taller vaseline with a white opalescent rim on a stem foot. Catalogue says one tureen chipped. 'EYE GLASSES' in the catalogue means eye baths. Update after Lens: the cat on nest is the same mould as a Mosser Glass (Cambridge, Ohio) miniature cat on nest sold on eBay; the lacy scalloped bases on all four look like one maker's series, most likely Mosser miniatures (Boyd makes similar mini turkey and Scottie salts). Made from the 1970s onward, not antique.
marks_seen: Inside the nest bases there are small pale oval marks (look like sticker residue or a moulded mark, not readable at this resolution). Left eye bath foot has a faint moulded mark underneath, not legible. No maker name readable.
google_searches: Google Lens on photo 2 (hen and turkey on nest): visual matches were Boyd and Mosser vaseline mini hen-on-nest salts (Etsy, WorthPoint, Invaluable 'Vintage Mosser Vaseline Glass Mini Hen On Nest', Curiosity Corners AU 'Vintage Vaseline Uranium Glass Hen On A Nest Mosser', Albion 'RARE URANIUM GLASS DOGGY ON BASKET TRINKET POT'). Identified the cat as the exact Mosser miniature cat on nest mould (lacy scalloped base) from eBay listing 257828611092.

resale_estimate: Sold individually on eBay to US collectors: Mosser vaseline mini cat A$150-190, mini hen A$150-230, turkey A$70-130, Scottie/dog A$35-70, eye baths A$60-110 each (opal-rim one may be a modern Rosso/Mosser piece, A$40-100). One tureen is chipped (unknown which). The opal-rim eye bath may be a new Rosso Wholesale/Mosser piece. Prices depend on selling to US buyers; postage from Tasmania eats into small items. Other bidders likely know the Mosser/Boyd collector market.
viewing_check: Find which tureen is chipped and how bad. Check under each base for a moulded M (Mosser), B in diamond (Boyd) or D in heart/triangle (Degenhart). Check the eye bath feet for maker marks (an R, or Guernsey). UV torch to confirm all glow.

identification: Heavy hand-blown sculptural 'bird/horn' centrepiece bowl, about 20 cm high: two flared ribbed lobes rising from a solid uranium (vaseline) green core, cased in clear glass, rims shading to amber/honey, on a thick round clear-and-green foot. Optic-ribbed walls. Style is mid-century Czech (Bohemian) art glass of the 1960s-70s, the type attributed to Josef Hospodka for Chribska glassworks or Prachen/Sklo Union; Murano Sommerso is the other possibility.

resale_estimate: A$150-250 in Australia (Marketplace, Gumtree or a Tasmanian/Melbourne natural history auction such as Lawsons or Philips). Unlikely to beat A$250 uncased with no maker.
doubts: No Australian sale of a ptarmigan found; all comparables are US or UK. US prices converted at about 1.53 AUD per USD and UK at about 2.03 AUD per GBP. Overseas buyers pay more for cased antique work (the Inverness piece), but ours shows no case or maker label. Legal: rock ptarmigan is IUCN Least Concern and is not on any CITES appendix, and it is not an Australian native, so selling it within Australia is lawful and the EPBC Act wildlife-trade permits for export should not apply. But eBay bans most bird taxidermy, couriers and airlines often refuse it, and the buyer country's biosecurity rules apply (US: game birds are not covered by the Migratory Bird Treaty Act, but USFWS and agricultural import rules still apply). In practice it is a local-pickup sale. Current bid is A$110 and 22% premium applies, so at A$150 hammer you pay about A$183 and break even at best.
viewing_check: Look under the base for a taxidermist label or import paperwork (an old British or Scandinavian label would add value). Check for moth or insect damage (bare patches, frass under the bird), loose feathers, cracked feet and fading. Smell for mould.

identification: Barsony (Sydney, 1950s) figural TV lamp model FL41 'Drum Beat of Trinidad', 35 cm: black glazed hula/Caribbean dancer with drum under her arm, standing in front of a fan of green palm fronds, hand-painted cream, red, gold and green details, lamp fitting behind the fronds. The mould, pose, palm fan and painted pattern match exactly the genuine Barsony FL41 sold on eBay 26 Oct 2026 (same 35 cm height). So it is the Barsony FL41 design, not just 'Barsony style'; whether this example is a genuine Barsony or an unmarked copy depends on the base mark.
marks_seen: Base (photo 3, enhanced): glazed black, two holes (lamp fitting and vent), small rubber foot; no legible Barsony name or FL41 number. Faint marks in the glaze at the centre of the base are not readable in the photo. Paint wear (white flecks) around the base rim.

I found no sale of this exact America's Cup 1987 decanter anywhere, so the theme premium is unknown; the World Cup prices are lifted by football collectors and should not be used as the target. Fill level, seal and contents strength cannot be checked from photos; ceramic decanters can evaporate or leak. viewing_check: Check the capsule and cork are intact and unbroken, gently shake or weigh it to confirm it is full (a full 75cl ceramic is heavy, about 1.5 kg or more), and look for a neck or back label giving volume and strength. Check for chips or crazing on the ceramic and cracks in the plastic case.

identification: Oil on board or canvas, portrait format, framed in a modern gilt moulding with grey linen slip. Evening/dusk bush river scene: tall dead eucalypts with hanging bark at left, dense bush, yellow sunset band, still water with reflections in the foreground. Catalogue: ERNEST CHRISTMAS ATTRIBUTED OIL EVENING ON THE YARRA RIVER H-35 W-25 CM. Style (dark tonal bush river at dusk, gold sky band) is consistent with the late Victorian Australian bush-river genre that Ernest William Christmas (1863-1918, born Adelaide, worked Victoria/NSW, then NZ and Hawaii) painted, but it is a common genre. Ernest Christmas was not a Tasmanian painter, the lot note has that wrong.
marks_seen: Only one photo exists (1635098_1.jpg, 450x600; _2 to _8 return 404). Enlarged 3x and zoomed both lower corners and the lower edge: no signature or initials visible in the paint. Upper corners and edges also show no visible signature at this resolution. No back of the painting is photographed, so the title Evening on the Yarra River probably comes from a back label or inscription not shown.

Attributed Ernest W Christmas, Renmark landscape, oil on canvas 83 x 56 cm, passed with no estimate. Only 'attributed' entry found with an outcome; shows attributed works struggle.

resale_estimate: If genuinely initialled E W C (or signed) and period: A$250-450 hammer at a capital-city art auction, going on four verified 2025 results for small signed or initialled river scenes (A$260, A$425, A$460) plus A$380 in 2020. As photographed (no visible signature or initials, attributed only): A$80-150, decorative value plus a punt on the attribution.
doubts: Only one photo, front only, 450x600. No signature or initials could be seen in either lower corner or along the edges even at 3x, but they could be small and dark in the shadowed foreground, which is where Christmas usually put E W C. No photo of the back, so the title and any label are unseen. 'Attributed' from a general auction house means they could not confirm it. The bush river at dusk with dead trees and gold sky band fits his 1890s Murray/Victorian work but was a very common genre. Verdict 'raises' only applies if initials are found: a confirmed E W C piece this size has been making A$260-460 at Gibson's in 2025, so A$115 would be conservative and A$200 hammer (A$244 with 22% BP) still leaves room. Without initials, A$115 is about the limit and A$60-80 is safer.
viewing_check: Look hard (with a torch, angled) at the lower left and lower right corners for E W C or E.W. Christmas and a date like /90 to /95. Check the back for a label, inscription 'Evening on the Yarra' or a dealer stamp, the board or canvas type (period academy board or 1890s canvas, not modern hardboard), and craquelure consistent with 130 years. If initials and a period support are there, A$200 max; if nothing, cap at A$60-80.
searches_tried: Invaluable artist sold page (47 lots, 2002-2025) with prices read on Gibson's and Lawsons' own lot pages; AASD and artrecord (prices paywalled, used only for lot lists incl. Leonard Joel 'attributed' River Sunset 34.5 x 26 cm, price not visible); LiveAuctioneers search (no Christmas painter hits); Leski and Davidson own sites (hash lookup 404); Google/web search for attributed Christmas sales. eBay not tried for this lot (fine art at this level does not trade there in volume).
